translation_en: Ibn Shihab said: ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Malik al-Mudliji, who was the nephew of Suraqah ibn Malik ibn Ju‘shum, informed me that his father told him that he heard Suraqah ibn Ju‘shum say: Messengers of the unbelievers of Quraysh came to us offering the blood-price for each of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, and Abu Bakr, to anyone who killed or captured either of them. While I was sitting in an assembly of my people, Banu Mudlij, one of them came and stood over us while we were seated. He said, ‘Suraqah, I have just seen some dark figures on the coast. I think they are Muhammad and his companions.’ Suraqah said: I knew that it was them, but I said to him, ‘They are not those people. You saw so-and-so and so-and-so, who went off before our eyes.’ Then I stayed in the gathering for a while. I got up, went inside, and told my servant girl to bring out my horse and hold it for me behind a hill. I took my spear and went out through the back of the house. I lowered its spearhead to the ground and held the shaft low until I reached my horse and mounted it. I urged her forward and she carried me at a fast pace until I came close to them. My horse stumbled and I fell from it. I got up, reached into my quiver, took out the divining arrows, and drew lots to find out whether I should harm them or not. The result was what I disliked. I mounted my horse anyway, disregarding the arrows, and she carried me forward. When I could hear the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, reciting, and he did not turn around while Abu Bakr kept turning around, my horse’s forelegs sank into the ground up to the knees. I fell from her. Then I urged her on, and she rose, barely able to pull her forelegs out. When she stood upright, a cloud of dust rose into the sky from the tracks of her forelegs, like smoke. I drew lots again with the divining arrows, and the result was what I disliked. So I called out to them, asking for a guarantee of safety. They stopped. I mounted my horse and came to them. After what I had experienced when I was held back from reaching them, I felt that the cause of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, would prevail. I said to him, ‘Your people have offered a blood-price for you.’ I told them what people intended to do to them and offered them provisions and supplies. They did not accept anything from me or ask me for anything. They only said, ‘Keep our whereabouts secret.’ I asked him to write me a document guaranteeing my safety. He ordered ‘Amir ibn Fuhayrah to write it on a piece of leather. Then the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, continued on his way. Ibn Shihab said: ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr informed me that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, met al-Zubayr among a group of Muslims who were merchants returning from Syria. Al-Zubayr gave the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, and Abu Bakr white garments. The Muslims in Madinah heard that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, had set out from Makkah. Every morning they went to the lava field and waited for him until the midday heat drove them back. One day they returned after waiting a long time. When they had gone back to their homes, a Jewish man climbed onto one of their fortresses for something he was looking at. He saw the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, and his companions, dressed in white, with the mirage shimmering around them. The Jewish man could not help shouting at the top of his voice, ‘Arabs, here is your great one whom you have been waiting for!’ The Muslims rushed to take up their weapons and met the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, at the back of the lava field. He turned to the right with them until he stopped among Banu ‘Amr ibn ‘Awf. This was on a Monday in the month of Rabi‘ al-Awwal. Abu Bakr stood to greet the people, while the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, sat silently. The Ansar who came and had not seen the Messenger of Allah began greeting Abu Bakr, until the sun reached the Messenger of Allah. Abu Bakr came forward and shaded him with his cloak. Then the people recognized the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him. He stayed among Banu ‘Amr ibn ‘Awf for a little more than ten nights. The mosque that was founded upon piety was established, and the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, prayed in it. Then he mounted his riding camel and travelled, with the people walking alongside him, until it knelt at the place of the Messenger’s mosque in Madinah. At that time some Muslim men were praying there. It was a drying yard for dates belonging to two orphan boys, Suhayl and Sahl, who were under the care of As‘ad ibn Zurarah. When his riding camel knelt, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, ‘This will be the stopping place, if Allah wills.’ Then the Messenger of Allah called the two boys and negotiated with them for the drying yard so that he could make it a mosque. They said, ‘No. We give it to you, Messenger of Allah.’ Then he built it as a mosque. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, began carrying bricks with them as they built it, saying as he carried the bricks, ‘This load is unlike the load of Khaybar; this is more virtuous with our Lord and purer.’ He also said, ‘O Allah, the reward is the reward of the Hereafter, so have mercy on the Ansar and the Emigrants.’ He recited lines of poetry by a Muslim man whose name was not given to me. Ibn Shihab said: We have not received any reports that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, recited a complete line of poetry apart from these lines.’
